questions.question: A boat can travel at a speed of 30 km/h in still water. If the flow of the stream is 2 km/h. How long will it take by the boat to travel 56 km upstream?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Upstream Speed = Speed of boat − Speed of stream

Upstream Speed = 30 − 2 = 28 km/h

Time = Distance ÷ Upstream Speed = 56 ÷ 28 = 2 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 2 hours.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of boat in still water = 30 km/h

Speed of stream = 2 km/h

Distance to travel upstream = 56 km

 
 

 Distance = 56 km

 Stream = 2 km/h

 Upstream Speed = 30 - 2 = 28 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Upstream Speed = Boat Speed − Stream Speed

Time = Distance ÷ Upstream Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Upstream speed = 30 − 2 = 28 km/h

⇒ Time taken = 56 ÷ 28

⇒ Time taken = 2 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 2 hours.**

**__Additional Information__**

Downstream Speed

When the boat travels along the direction of the stream, Downstream Speed = Boat Speed + Stream Speed.

Boat Speed in Still Water

If Downstream Speed (D) and Upstream Speed (U) are given, Boat Speed = (D + U) ÷ 2.

Stream Speed

If Downstream Speed (D) and Upstream Speed (U) are given, Stream Speed = (D − U) ÷ 2.

questions.question: A tradesman marked the price of his goods to earn a profit of 20% after giving a discount of 20%. Marked price is how much percentage more than the cost price?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Profit percent = 20%

Discount percent = 20%

**Concept:**

If an item is sold at a profit of P% after giving a discount of D%, then the marked price (M) is given by the formula M = [100/(100 - D)] × (100 + P).

**Solution:**

⇒ Marked price = [100/(100 - 20)] × (100 + 20)

⇒ Marked price = (100/80) × 120 = 150

**Therefore, the marked price is 50% more than the cost price.**

questions.question: The traffic lights at two different road crossings change after every 54 sec and 76 sec, respectively. If they change simultaneously at 10:15:00 hours, then find the time at which they will change again simultaneously.
questions.solution:
**Given**

The time period of first light = 54 seconds

The time period of the second light = 76 seconds

**Concept:**

Two events with different periods will coincide again after a time equal to the least common multiple (LCM) of their periods.

**Solution:**

⇒ LCM of 54 and 76 = 2052 seconds = 34 minutes 12 second

⇒ Add this to the start time of 10:15:00 + 00:34:12

**Therefore, the lights will change again simultaneously at 10:49:12.**

questions.question: In a class there are 80 students. Average weight of girls is 40 kg and average weight of boys is 50 kg. If number of boys is 50, then what will be the average weight of class?

Total students = 80

The average weight of girls = 40 kg

The average weight of boys = 50 kg

Number of boys = 
50

The average weight of the class is total weight of the class divided by the total students.

**Solution:**

⇒ Total weight of boys = Number of boys × Average weight of boys = 50 × 50 = 2500 kg

questions.question: P, Q, and R working separately can do a piece of work in 50, 100, and 300 days respectively. If they work on alternate days, P works on the first day, Q works on the second day, R works on the third day and then again P works on the fourth day and so on, then in how many days, the work will be completed?
questions.solution:
**Given**

P can do the work in 50 days

Q can do the work in 100 days

R can do the work in 300 days

**Concept:**

Work done is the inverse of the time taken to complete the work. Total work done in one cycle (3 days) is the sum of work done by P, Q, and R in one day.

**Solution:**

⇒ Work done by P in one day = 1/50

⇒ Work done by Q in one day = 1/100

⇒ Work done by R in one day = 1/300

⇒ Total work done in one cycle (3 days) = (1/50) + (1/100) + (1/300) = 1/30

⇒ Time taken to complete one whole work = 3/(1/30) = 90 days

**Therefore, the work will be completed in 90 days.**

questions.question: If the difference between the simple interest and the compound interest, compounding annually on a certain sum borrowed for 2 years at 8% per annum is ₹512, then find the sum borrowed (in ₹).
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Difference between simple and compound interest = ₹512

Time = 2 years

Rate of interest = 8%

**Concept:**

The difference between compound interest and simple interest for two years is given by the formula = P × (R/100)².

**Solution:**

⇒ Principal (P) = Difference between SI and CI/(R/100)²

⇒ P = ₹512/(8/100)²

⇒ P = ₹512/64 × 10000

⇒ P = ₹80,000

**Therefore, the sum borrowed is ₹80,000.**

questions.question: The population of a village is 68000. It increases at the rate of 5 percent in the first year and decreases at the rate of 10 percent per annum for the next 2 years. What will be the population of the village after 3 years?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Initial population = 68000

First-year increase = 5%

Second and third-year decrease = 10% each year

**Concept:**

Population change can be calculated using the formula: Final = Initial × (1 + change/100) for each year.

**Solution:**

⇒ After first year, population = Initial population × (1 + increase/100) = 68000 × (1 + 5/100) = 71400

⇒ After second year, population = First year population × (1 - decrease/100) = 71400 × (1 - 10/100) = 64260

⇒ After third year, population = Second year population × (1 - decrease/100) = 64260 × (1 - 10/100) = 57834

**Therefore, the population of the village after 3 years will be 57834.**

questions.question: The greatest 4-digit number divisible by 36 and 45 is subtracted from 10,000. Find the result.
questions.solution:
**Given **

The target number is divisible by 36 and 45

**Concept:**

The least common multiple (LCM) gives the smallest number that is divisible by the two numbers. The greatest 4-digit number divisible by the LCM is found by subtracting the remainder when 9999 (the largest 4-digit number) is divided by the LCM.

**Solution:**

⇒ LCM of 36 and 45 = 180

⇒ The largest 4-digit number divisible by 180 = 9999 - (9999 mod 180) = 9999 - 99 = 9900

⇒ Result = 10,000 - 9900 = 100

**Therefore, the result is 100.**

questions.question: What is the mean proportional between 121 and 169?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Two numbers: 121 and 169.

**Concept:**

The mean proportional or geometric mean of two numbers a and b is given by sqrt{(a × b)}.

**Solution:**

⇒ Mean proportional = sqrt{(121 × 169)}

⇒ Mean proportional = sqrt{11²×13²}

⇒ Mean proportional = 11 × 13

⇒ Mean proportional = 143

**Therefore, the mean proportional between 121 and 169 is 143.**

questions.question: When 40 is subtracted from 40 percent of a number then we get 40. Find the number.
questions.solution:
**Given**

40 subtracted from 40% of a number equals 40

**Concept:**

This problem can be solved by setting up and solving a simple equation.

**Solution:**

Let the number be x.

⇒ 40% of x - 40 = 40

⇒ 0.4x - 40 = 40

⇒ 0.4x = 80

⇒ x = 80/0.4

⇒ x = 200

**Therefore, the number is 200.**

questions.question: The difference between the 110% of a number and 94.5% of the same number is 34.1. What is the original number?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Difference between 110% and 94.5% of a number = 34.1

**Concept:**

This can be solved by setting up and solving a simple algebraic equation.

**Solution:**

Let the original number be x.

⇒ 110% of x - 94.5% of x = 34.1

⇒ (110/100)x - (94.5/100)x = 34.1

⇒ (15.5/100)x = 34.1

⇒ x = (34.1 × 100)/15.5

⇒ x = 220

**Therefore, the original number is 220.**

questions.question: The successive discounts of 10%, 30% and 25% is equivalent to a single discount of _______ (correct to a nearest whole number).
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Successive discounts: 10%, 30%, 25%

**Concept Used:**

Successive discounts can be calculated by

Final discount = 1 - (1 - D₁)(1 - D₂)(1 - D₃)

**Solution:**

Final discount = 1 - (1 - 0.10)(1 - 0.30)(1 - 0.25)

⇒ Final discount = 1 - (0.9)(0.7)(0.75)

⇒ Final discount = 1 - 0.4725

⇒ Final discount = 0.5275

⇒ Final discount = 52.75% ≈ 53%

**∴ The successive discounts of 10%, 30%, and 25% are equivalent to a single discount of 53%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Formula Used:**

Successive discount can be calculated by

Equivalent Discount = D1 + D2 - (D₁times D₂)/(100)

**Calculation:**

Successive discounts of 10% and 30%

⇒ Equivalent Discount = 10 + 30 - (10times 30)/(100) = 37%

Successive discounts of 37% and 25%

⇒ Final Discount = 37 + 25 - (37×25)/(100)

⇒ Final Discount = 62 - 9.25 = 52.75 ≈ 53%

∴ The successive discounts of 10%, 30%, and 25% are equivalent to a single discount of 53%.

questions.question: There are 45 boxes which have an average weight of 52 g. Some boxes are blue, while others are green. If five blue boxes having average weight of 40 g, and eight green boxes having average weight of 43 g, are added, then what is the average weight (in g) now?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Initial number of boxes = 45

Initial average weight = 52 g

Additional blue boxes = 5 with average weight 40 g

Additional green boxes = 8 with average weight 43 g

**Concept:**

The new average weight after adding the boxes can be calculated by dividing the total weight by the total number of boxes.

**Solution:**

⇒ Total initial weight = 45 boxes × 52 g/box = 2340 g

⇒ Total weight of additional blue boxes = 5 boxes × 40 g/box = 200 g

⇒ Total weight of additional green boxes = 8 boxes × 43 g/box = 344 g

⇒ New total weight = 2340 g + 200 g + 344 g = 2884 g

⇒ Total number of boxes = 45 + 5 + 8 = 58 boxes

⇒ New average weight = 2884 g / 58 boxes = 49.72 g/box

**Therefore, the new average weight of the boxes is 49.72 g.**

questions.question: A heap of wheat is in the form of a cone of diameter 30 m and height 8 m. How much canvas cloth will be required to just cover the heap (take π = 3.14)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Radius (r) = 30 ÷ 2 = 15 m, Height (h) = 8 m.

Using the Pythagorean triplet (8, 15, 17), the slant height (l) = 17 m.

Canvas required = Curved Surface Area = πrl

⇒ Area = 3.14 × 15 × 17 = 3.14 × 255 = 800.7

**∴ The correct answer is 800.7 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Diameter of the base of the cone (d) = 30 m

⇒ Radius (r) = d ÷ 2 = 30 ÷ 2 = 15 m

Height of the cone (h) = 8 m

Value of π = 3.14

 

 

 
 
• 
 h = 8 m
 
• 
 r = 15 m
 l = 17 m
 Canvas Area = Curved Surface Area

**Formula Used:**

Slant height of a cone (l) = √(r² + h²)

Curved Surface Area (CSA) of a cone = πrl

**Calculations:**

⇒ First, find the slant height (l) of the conical heap:

⇒ l = √(15² + 8²)

⇒ l = √(225 + 64)

⇒ l = √289 = 17 m

⇒ The area of the canvas required to just cover the heap is equal to its Curved Surface Area.

⇒ Canvas required = πrl

⇒ Canvas required = 3.14 × 15 × 17

⇒ Canvas required = 3.14 × 255

⇒ Canvas required = 800.7 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 800.7 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of a Cone

The total surface area includes both the curved surface and the flat circular base: TSA = πrl + πr² = πr(l + r).

Volume of a Cone

The volume of a cone is exactly one-third the volume of a cylinder that has the same base radius and height: Volume = (1/3)πr²h.

Pythagorean Triplets

Using standard right-angle triangle triplets such as (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), and (8, 15, 17) helps in quickly finding the missing side lengths in 2D and 3D geometry problems.
